## The signal and the task

![](assets/spectrogram_comb.png){width="100%"}

::: {.small}
Each rotor is a harmonic comb spaced by its speed $r_i(t)$, on a broadband floor. The task: from one microphone, $\hat{\mathbf r}[\tau] \approx \mathbf r(\tau/f_{\mathrm r})$, four speeds per frame at $f_{\mathrm r} = 31.25$ Hz (the STFT frame rate; the MD2 telemetry has no more).
:::

::: {.notes}
Frame 24 of the frozen real split: DREGON room 1, mic 0, 8 s cruise. Right panel overlays k·r_i for k ≤ 10 from the telemetry. Motivation in one line if asked: rotor-conditioned suppression (Gulli et al. 2025) needs these speeds; telemetry is not always there.
:::

## HRSPNet

::: {.content-visible when-format="revealjs"}
![](assets/fig_hrspnet.png){width="36%" fig-align="center"}
:::
::: {.content-visible unless-format="revealjs"}
![](assets/fig_hrspnet.png){width="46%"}
:::

::: {.notes}
Real MD2 validation clip (FLY124, frame 264), pyramid + rate ConvLSTM checkpoint. (a) four STFTs on one hop, range doubling, same bins per level. (b) harmonic proportionally dilated convolution + rate ConvLSTM. (c) the four per-rotor salience layers as the model emits them. (d, e) CRF readout, tracks against telemetry (identity-order MAE 0.93 rev/s on this clip).
:::

## How it reads a comb: pyramid + HPDC

![](assets/hpdc_fans.png){width="88%"}

::: {.small}
Output on a **linear rate grid** (0.977 rev/s, 307 bins to 300 rev/s); the harmonic dilated convolution of HPPNet becomes a *proportionally* dilated one. Four per-rotor layers, permutation-invariant cross-entropy, CRF path per layer.
:::

::: {.notes}
Levels: 16384/8192/4096/2048 at hop 512, kept to 1.2·2^l kHz. Tap k of rate g reads kg from the finest level which holds it, linear interpolation, one (C_out, C_in) weight per tap shared across g; implemented as a gather with a fused Triton kernel (A100: pyramid step 498 → 293 ms). Taps currently read below 4.8 kHz (levels 0–2); level 3 enters via fusion.
:::

## How it tracks: a recurrence that follows the rotor

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
![](assets/lstm_cartoon.png){width="100%"}
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
![](assets/slew_hist.png){width="100%"}
:::
:::

::: {.small}
Rotors move between bins continuously; a throttle punch is 15 rev/s per frame. The hidden-to-gate map is a 33-tap convolution along rate ($\pm 16$ bins), sized from the telemetry.
:::

::: {.notes}
Histogram: per-frame |Δr| over the validation telemetry (motors on); median ~0.2 rev/s per frame at 31.25 fps, 99th percentile ~2; the sustained 15 rev/s/frame punch is in the DREGON up/down training recording. FreqGroupLSTM is a cruise denoiser, not a tracker.
:::

## Where it stands: real-data training, no synthetic pretraining

![](assets/bars_current.png){width="80%"}

::: {.small}
Both rate-ConvLSTM variants beat the best adapted HPPNet (2.27) and the best regressor (2.99) from real data alone. These are the numbers *before* synthetic pretraining; the pretraining arms for HRSPNet are running.
:::

::: {.notes}
Unified panel, val/real_overall, one seed: CQT k≤9 + ConvLSTM 2.16, pyramid k≤32 + ConvLSTM 2.17 (docs/handoff-pyramid-harmonic.md §2). HPPNet-L2 2.27 is the frozen-split number under the earlier 1 s recipe (2.25 on this panel as nv2_mixed_hppnet_l2). Conv+BiGRU 2.99 = real_r4_scv2_unified. Differences of 0.1 are within single-seed noise; the 0.3–0.8 gaps are not.
:::

## Why: it is multi-pitch tracking, but not music

![](assets/tracks_vs_pianoroll.png){width="100%"}

::: {.small}
| rotors | notes | what it breaks in a music model |
|---|---|---|
| always present, continuous pitch | on/off events on a semitone grid | onset/offset heads, per-bin recurrence |
| four within one octave, often $<1$ rev/s apart, crossing | simultaneous semitones are rare | one shared salience map on a log axis |
:::

## Why per-rotor layers: a shared map cannot even encode the tracks

![](assets/encode_decode.png){width="74%"}

::: {.small}
Telemetry → one 48-bin/octave map → peak-pick + assign, no model in the loop: pairs closer than one bin merge. On the DREGON validation clips this floor is **8.2 rev/s**; four per-rotor layers on a linear grid return the tracks exactly.
:::

::: {.content-visible when-format="revealjs"}
![](assets/bars_output.png){width="56%"}
:::
::: {.content-visible unless-format="revealjs"}
![](assets/bars_output.png){width="60%"}
:::

::: {.notes}
8.2 rev/s and 2e-16 rev/s: encode–decode test of the paper's appendix (55 % of DREGON frames have a pair < 1 Hz apart). Bars: Block S of paper-regime-matrix.md, one seed each. Basic Pitch has no harmonic device → not carried further.
:::

## Why the harmonic range: the motor lines live at high orders

![](assets/rate_sync_spectrum.png){width="100%"}

::: {.small}
DREGON's motors put lines at orders 14, 42, 70 (brightest) — far above HPPNet's nine. A rate difference $\delta$ is $k\delta$ Hz at order $k$: close rotors separate there. Extending to $k \le 84$: CQT model 2.45 → 2.31 (no recurrence).
:::

::: {.notes}
Rate-synchronous spectrum: frame 24, rotor 0, 16384-point STFT resampled to order axis per frame and averaged, local floor removed. The wide bumps at k ≈ 10–20 are the aerodynamic lines with their pedestal (haystacking). The k ≈ 70 line is the one that becomes a rotor-identity cue (next slide).
:::

## Why the pyramid: resolution where the harmonics are

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="46%"}
![](assets/resolution_curves.png){width="100%"}
:::
::: {.column width="54%"}
![](assets/bars_taps.png){width="100%"}
:::
:::

::: {.small}
Rate resolution at order $k$ is $\Delta f/k$: the CQT throws the $1/k$ lever away, a single STFT smears under slew; the pyramid keeps both. Zeroing taps in the trained models shows the pyramid *does* read $k = 31$–60 (worth 1.1 rev/s). Its top level hurts on DREGON only: the $k \approx 70$ line belongs to a different rotor in room 2 (training) than in room 1 (validation), and room 2's command labels are 1–3 % off — a data problem, not a front-end one. HRSPNet therefore reads taps below 4.8 kHz.
:::

::: {.notes}
Tap ablation: handoff §3, no retraining. Without level-3 taps the pyramid conv model is 2.22 vs CQT 2.31. The slew/resolution balance: T*_k = 1/sqrt(k ṙ), optimum Δf ∝ f^{1/2}; a VQT would realise it exactly (docs/vqt-frontend-idea.md) — only if asked.
:::

## Why generative pretraining: no model transfers between drones

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
![](assets/bars_transfer.png){width="100%"}
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](assets/genmodel_overview.png){width="100%"}
:::
:::

::: {.small}
Two drones with telemetry exist (DREGON, public; MD2, ours). Trained on one, a model fails on the other; one flight of the second drone closes the gap — coverage, not capacity. Hence a probabilistic generative model: a state-space law for the four speed trajectories (fitted to 7 rigs' telemetry) and a harmonic-plus-broadband law for the audio given them (fitted to recordings); every rendered clip is labeled exactly.
:::

## The model is faithful, and pretraining on it works

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="34%"}
![](assets/gen_traj_real_vs_sampled.png){width="92%"}

![](assets/gen_noise_real_vs_sampled.png){width="92%"}
:::
::: {.column width="66%"}
![](assets/bars_pretrain.png){width="100%"}
:::
:::

::: {.small}
On the previous models: synthetic-only pretraining reads real audio without fine-tuning (6.5–8 rev/s); pretrain → fine-tune beats real-only training (2.23 vs 2.99; 2.11 vs 2.27); mixing is weaker; static and stochastic combs do not transfer (9.5–10.7 alone, no gain as warm start). **HRSPNet pretraining arms: in progress.**
:::

::: {.notes}
Parity gate: real-trained HPPNet reads the renders at 1.82 (DREGON) / 1.62 (MD2) rev/s against bars 2.19 / 3.03. Simpler generators: static comb 9.50 alone, 2.74 as warm start (= real-only 2.77 under that recipe); stochastic comb 10.74; HPPNet on static comb 66. Sources: noise-v2-transfer.md, paper tab:nv2 / tab:ablation.
:::
